case_studies.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
case_studies.abstract: As AI coding agents become more autonomous, they increasingly ship code iteratively, with the codebase persisting across sessions. This persistence creates a new attack surface: a misaligned or prompt-injected agent can distribute attacks across pull requests (PRs) and time its payload for the PR with the best natural cover. To study the resulting dynamics, we introduce Iterative VibeCoding, a setting for AI control, the study of safely deploying capable but potentially untrusted AI. In Iterative VibeCoding, a coding agent builds software over a sequence of PRs in a persistent codebase while p
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of AI coding agents potentially introducing attacks into codebases over time, the authors built a setting called Iterative VibeCoding to study this, and the result highlights a new attack surface in persistent codebases. The study focuses on safely deploying potentially untrusted AI in coding tasks. This research is relevant to securing cloud infrastructure where AI agents are used for coding tasks.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you use AI coding agents in your cloud infrastructure, here is what to do: step 1, review your codebase for potential distributed attacks, step 2, implement checks on AI-generated pull requests, step 3, monitor your codebase for unusual patterns across sessions.
case_studies.score_reasoning: While not directly an IT paper, it has IT relevance due to its focus on AI control and deployment. However, its real-world impact is limited and not actionable within 90 days.

case_studies.title: Conversational Query Engine for Mixed-Modality Heterogeneous Enterprise Data Sources
case_studies.abstract: Enterprise business intelligence queries span structured warehouses and unstructured document repositories -- modalities with fundamentally different access methods, cost profiles, and correctness semantics. Existing AI-enabled interfaces force users to select the right tool: NL2SQL systems cannot reason over slide decks, and RAG pipelines lack access to live warehouse tables. We present COGNI, a production conversational BI system that treats natural-language analytics as a heterogeneous query processing problem, organized as four architectural layers. First, an indexing layer implements slid
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of querying different types of data sources in a business intelligence setting by building a conversational query engine called COGNI, which can process natural-language queries across both structured and unstructured data. The result is a system that allows users to access various data sources using a single interface. The research focuses on business intelligence and data analysis, rather than cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on business intelligence and data analysis rather than cloud infrastructure management. If you manage business intelligence systems, you may be interested in exploring COGNI as a potential solution for querying heterogeneous data sources. However, for general IT infrastructure work, no specific action is required.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel and relevant system for querying heterogeneous enterprise data sources, but value to an IT engineer is limited given the focus on natural-language analytics and query processing. The system architecture is the most relevant aspect, with the indexing layer, query layer, and data integration modules.

case_studies.title: Beyond Adam: SOAP and Muon for Faster, Label-Efficient Training of Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
case_studies.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have become a hallmark of AI for scientific simulation. While efforts on new architectures and datasets have led to increasingly accurate and general models, the choice of optimizer for training has largely remained unexplored, defaulting to Adam and its variants in the community. Here, we implement and systematically compare a class of recently proposed matrix-structured optimizers, including Muon, SOAP, and the hybrid SOAP-Muon, for training NequIP and Allegro MLIP models. We find that these optimizers can substantially outperform Adam in both
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of slow training of machine learning interatomic potentials by introducing new optimizers, building on SOAP and Muon, which result in faster and more efficient training. The researchers built and compared new optimizers for training MLIP models, achieving better performance than the commonly used Adam optimizer. This research may lead to improvements in machine learning model training, but its direct impact on cloud infrastructure management is unclear.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on machine learning model training optimizers, but IT teams supporting ML workloads may be aware of potential improvements in model training efficiency in the future.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: 5 (purely academic), IT Relevance: 10 (optimizers for MLIPs not a direct concern for IT engineers), Value 90 Days: 20 (interesting but can't be applied directly)

case_studies.title: Carolina Guide: A Multi-Agent RAG System with Institutional Guardrails for Academic Policy Assistance
case_studies.abstract: University students often struggle to navigate complex academic policies, leading to advising bottlenecks and delayed access to critical information. Although large language models (LLMs) offer promise for automated assistance, their tendency toward hallucination and inability to enforce institutional constraints make them unsuitable for high-stakes policy guidance without careful architectural design. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of university students struggling to navigate complex academic policies by building a retrieval-augmented generation system called Carolina Guide. The system helps with academic policy assistance and enforces institutional constraints. It's not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.score_reasoning: While Carolina Guide presents a unique approach to leveraging LLMs for policy assistance, its direct impact on IT infrastructure is limited to deployment considerations. The novelty lies in its application beyond typical LLM use cases. However, the potential for real-world application is limited and not directly actionable for IT engineers or consultants.

case_studies.title: Learning to Move Before Learning to Do: Task-Agnostic pretraining for VLAs
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are fundamentally bottlenecked by the scarcity of expert demonstrations -- triplets of observations, instructions, and actions that are costly to collect at scale. We argue that this bottleneck stems from conflating two distinct learning objectives: acquiring physical competence (how to move) and acquiring semantic alignment (what to do). Crucially, only the latter requires language supervision. Building on this Decomposition Hypothesis, we propose Task-Agnostic Pretraining (TAP), a two-stage framework that first learns transferable motor priors from cheap,
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of scarce expert demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action models by proposing a two-stage framework called Task-Agnostic Pretraining. The researchers built a framework that learns motor priors from cheap, language-unsupervised data and then fine-tunes on language-supervised data. The result is a more efficient way to train VLA models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on machine learning model training for Vision-Language-Action tasks, which is a specialized area of AI research.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper discusses a new approach to VLA model training but lacks IT relevance and real-world impact.
